title: Teaching Schillinger: Nat Shilkret and few pupils
summary: He got a teaching certificate, but had few pupils, among them Nat Shilkret.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And it seems more like an aptitude than a talent, in a way. I don't know if I'm splitting hairs semantically, you know.
So what eventually happened with it? That was --

Well, I'd pass it. But then all I could tell is -- I knew what I was -- I knew the course. I knew the techniques of it, and I was qualified, according to what they said, to passing the course. I got a certificate that I was qualified to teach it.
So teaching something like that, I mean, I try to

get pupils, but trying to get pupils is -- it's ridiculous. However, some guys knew that I was giving it, and I had one pupil who was -- he came over and he studied. I say that we talked it over, you know. I tried to try and give him my -- what I got out of it. But I said, 'You'll probably have to do the work,' and that's Nat Shilkret, Bubsie.
So he wasn't doing much, and he lives out near me. He used to come over once a week.
Well, it could have been. Yes, I guess it was, the '50s. And then I had a couple of kids, and they -- they had the money. They could pay. But they didn't have the stick-to-it-iveness.
You have to know how much two times two is, two times three. Kids today rather rely on the computer or the calculator.

So it wasn't going so well, so I didn't bother. But some guys would come around and stick it out and then come back awhile, very few, though, not enough to make a living, and I would get all interested in telling them a few of these things, because I could see where it could help them.
